title: Can AI diagnose you? What the studies show , and when a doctor should check
summary: AI diagnosis and symptom checker studies: accuracy in conversations, triage risks, how to use AI well, and when a FutureClinic doctor should check.
body_markdown:
## How to use AI well, and when a doctor should check


In a[March 2026 KFF poll](https://www.kff.org/health-information-and-trust/kff-tracking-poll-on-health-information-and-trust-use-of-ai-for-health-information-and-advice/) , 58% of adults using AI for physical health followed up with a doctor. AI helps explain terms, organize records (like[Glass for Patients](https://glass.health/patients/how-to-use-glass-for-patients) ), and list questions. In an[October 2026 Lancet study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42849491/) funded by Alphabet, when 98 patients chatted with Google's AMIE before an urgent visit, doctors said the transcript helped them prepare in 33 of 44 cases.


At FutureClinic, we believe AI is a tool for doctors and the human doctor is in charge of every case. Most health problems have nuance needing one-to-one attention, and only an expert can tell when an AI makes a mistake. Behind the scenes, our AI works like a chief resident: it asks the intake questions your doctor trained it to ask, gathers your history and photos, and prepares a summary you confirm before the doctor sees it, while never giving medical advice by itself.


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. They cover more than 60 specialties, generalists and specialists alike, and every doctor holds an MD, DO or MBBS degree, never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. Replies typically come within a few hours, almost always the same day or the next. You can message the same doctor over time in the same chat to adjust a dose, swap an irritating cream, or compare labs, and a dermatologist treating hair loss can treat your acne or eczema too. FutureClinic sells no medicines, and your doctor earns nothing extra for any prescription or test. If your doctor decides it's right for you, prescriptions go to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that deliver to your door, and for a stable medicine they can prescribe several months at once when safe. Insurance may cover the medicine at the pharmacy, FutureClinic helps with prior authorizations, and we text a discount coupon for the cash price. Doctors do not prescribe controlled medicines. With no subscription required, you pay $40 for the best-fit doctor or pick a doctor at their listed price, typically $20 to $100, and most offer an optional membership, typically $25 to $100 a month, for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.


## Having a FutureClinic doctor check your symptoms from ChatGPT or Claude


FutureClinic operates in 33 states and Washington, D.C., and your doctor must be licensed in the state you are in: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. If you do not see your state, try anyway as the list grows.


Start at[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) , connect[ChatGPT](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-real-doctor-to-chatgpt) or[Claude](https://futureclinic.com/blog/how-to-add-a-doctor-to-claude) at[https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) , or send` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt` to your AI app. Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want. See our[editorial standards](https://futureclinic.com/blog/editorial-standards) .
